title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — target is immediate/antecedent ('common') imputation as Vir doctus defines it
pass_a_gloss: Placeus now names his target after sparing mediate imputation: the immediate and antecedent kind Garrigues calls 'common.' On Cap. 1 §13, Adam's sin made not only Adam guilty but implicated the whole race contained in him seminaliter in the same reatus from the moment of the fall.
pass_b_english: But the immediate and antecedent imputation, which the learned man calls "common" and so describes in Cap. 1 §13: "The common imputation of Adam's sin," he says, "is that by which Adam's sin made not only him guilty, but also implicated the whole race, which was contained in him seminaliter and radicaliter, in the same guilt, already from the time when Adam fell."
source_text: sed immediatam & antecedentem, quam Vir doctus communem appellat & ita describit Cap. 1. §. xiii. Imputatio, inquit, peccati Adami communis est, qua peccatum Adami non ipsum modo reum fecit, sed etiam totum genus, quod in ipso seminaliter & radicaliter continebatur, eodem reatu implicuit, iam ab eo tempore, quo lapsus est Adam.
